root_cause.text: The `__do_adjtimex()` function incorrectly referenced the global core timekeeper (`tk_core`) instead of the passed-in timekeeper instance (`tkd`) when calling `tk_update_leap_state_all()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff replaces `tk_update_leap_state_all(&tk_core)` with `tk_update_leap_state_all(tkd)` in `__do_adjtimex()`, and the commit message explains that when `__do_adjtimex()` was introduced to handle auxiliary timekeepers, this reference to `tk_core` was not updated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the local timekeeper data pointer instead of the global core pointer to tk_update_leap_state_all in __do_adjtimex.
intent_record.what: Replaced the hardcoded global pointer '&tk_core' with the function parameter 'tkd' in the call to 'tk_update_leap_state_all'.
intent_record.how: Ensures that the leap state update is applied to the specific timekeeping data instance passed to the function rather than always defaulting to the global core instance.

Author: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@kernel.org>

    timekeeping: Make do_adjtimex() reusable
    
    Split out the actual functionality of adjtimex() and make do_adjtimex() a
    wrapper which feeds the core timekeeper into it and handles the result
    including audit at the call site.
    
    This allows to reuse the actual functionality for auxiliary clocks.
    
    Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutr
bic_trace_step.reason: In the newly introduced `__do_adjtimex()` function, the code incorrectly calls `tk_update_leap_state_all(&tk_core)` instead of using the passed-in `tkd` parameter (i.e., `tk_update_leap_state_all(tkd)`). This introduces the vulnerability where auxiliary clocks using this function will incorrectly update the global `tk_core` leap state.

Author: Anna-Maria Behnsen <anna-maria@linutronix.de>

    timekeeping: Rework do_adjtimex() to use shadow_timekeeper
    
    Updates of the timekeeper can be done by operating on the shadow timekeeper
    and afterwards copying the result into the real timekeeper. This has the
    advantage, that the sequence count write protected region is kept as small
    as possible.
    
    Convert do_adjtimex() to use
bic_trace_step.reason: On line 2708, the function calls `__do_adjtimex(txc, &ts, &tai, &ad)` without passing the shadow timekeeper `tks` (which is defined on line 2704). Because the shadow timekeeper is not passed to `__do_adjtimex()`, the latter function cannot operate on the shadow instance and instead incorrectly references the global `tk_core` directly, which is the root cause of the vulnerability.
